files navigation Inline Logs See what your code logs right next to the line that logged it. Start your app, your dev server or your tests in the VS Code terminal as you always do. Each console.log value shows at the end of its line, a crash shows in red on the line that threw and in the Problems panel, and each fetch or WebSocket message shows on the line that made it. Logs from pino, winston, consola and tslog land on the line that called them too. Free and open source. Nothing to set up and nothing leaves your machine. [](/lagudafuadtosin/inlinelogs/blob/main/images/screenshot.png) What it does The latest value at the end of the line that logged it, in grey. Warnings in yellow. Uncaught errors and unhandled rejections in red on the line that threw, and in the Problems panel. A line that ran more than once shows ×3 at the end. Hover it for the full value and each run with its time and value. A line with several calls, such as fetch(url).then((r) = console.log(r)), shows each call's newest value side by side, left to right. console.table, console.dir and console.trace too. The line shows the table's size and columns, the object, or the trace message. The hover shows the drawn table, the whole object, or the call stack. console.count, console.time and timeEnd, console.group and a failing console.assert, each on its own line. pino, winston, consola and tslog, on the line that called them, in their level's colour. Insert a console.log for the name under the cursor, and comment out, uncomment or remove every console call in a file. A log viewer in the bottom panel. Search it with the same words as Search Logs, or filter by level. Click an entry to jump to its line. Edit the file and values move with their lines. A line you change loses its old value. The status bar shows the entry count. Click it to pause and resume. While paused it says Paused. Network requests, WebSocket and EventSource messages and beacons on the line that made them: method, status, time and URL, with headers and bodies in the hover. Secrets are redacted. Copy a value as JSON, and export everything captured to a JSON or text file. Compare a value with the one before it from the same line, or any two values, in VS Code's diff editor. Search everything captured, from the command or the log viewer's own search box, and the Log Map, a tree of every file and line with a value. A value graph: objects and arrays drawn as boxes you can zoom, pan and fold. Code coverage in the gutter for Node and Deno apps, when you turn it on. items.author: lagudafuad
items.descZh: inlinelogs 是一个 VS Code 扩展，它允许开发者在代码行旁边直接内联显示 console.log 值、错误和网络请求，从而简化调试流程。核心功能包括在行尾实时显示最新值（灰色）、警告（黄色）和错误（红色），并支持 hover 查看完整历史记录和每次运行的时间戳。亮点在于其免费、本地化且无需配置的特性，所有数据处理都在本地完成，确保隐私安全；同时它兼容 pino、winston 等多种日志库，并提供日志查看器、导出、值比较和代码覆盖等高级功能。适用场景主要是开发者在 Node.js 或 Deno 环境中频繁使用 console.log 进行调试时，能显著提高效率。
items.quote: 在 VS Code 中，您可以在代码旁查看 console.log 的值、错误和请求。
items.titleZh: Show HN: 行内日志，将 console.log 的值显示在 VS Code 中你的代码旁边

items.title: Show HN: Muxscape A graphical SSH client built on tmux
items.desc: description: A modern SSH client that turns persistent tmux sessions into clickable tabs and panes. Connect to your servers, manage your work graphically, and pick up exactly where you left off. title: Muxscape: Your servers. Your terminals. One workspace. image: https://muxscape.com/og.png [Skip to content](main) The SSH workspace that never closes. Your servers. Your terminals. One workspace. A modern SSH client that turns persistent tmux sessions into clickable tabs and panes. Connect to your servers, manage your work graphically, and pick up exactly where you left off. [Download for Windows(alpha)](https://github.com/CubezCStys/muxscape/releases/download/v0.1.0alpha.1/Muxscape%5F0.1.0%5Fx64setup.exe) [View on GitHub](https://github.com/CubezCStys/muxscape) Free. Windows alpha. Works with the SSH and tmux your servers already have. A real session: 22 tmux windows on one server, a second server below it. Tabs are tmux windows Click window 17 instead of remembering it. Split, drag, rename, close: each one is a real tmux command. Nothing stops when you leave Close the app or lose WiFi. Your builds, servers and agents keep running on the server. Come back to exactly that Muxscape reconnects and rebuilds every tab and pane from what tmux reports. Everything tmux does, without the keyboard gymnastics. 1. Twenty windows. One click each. Your existing tmux windows become tabs. Split, resize, rename and close panes with the mouse; every action is a real tmux command, so a plain tmux attach sees the same thing. Drag a divider to resize a split Doubleclick a tab to rename the window Drag a tab out into its own window 2. Find anything, fast. The quick switcher fuzzyfinds every window and session across your servers. Twenty windows stops being a memory test. Ctrl+Shift+P jump to any window or session Alt+1…9 and Ctrl+Tab between tabs Ctrl+Shift+F find text in a pane 3. Fullscreen programs look right. Each pane is its own terminal, drawn at exactly the size tmux uses. htop, editors and TUIs render as they would in a local terminal. 4. Your dev server, in your browser. Start a dev server and Muxscape notices the localhost:5173 it prints. One click forwards it over your SSH connection and opens it. The Ports panel shows what's listening, what it is and which pane started it. Forwards listen on your machine's loopback only Pin a forward and it comes back on every connect 5. All your servers, side by side. Each server keeps its own connection and sessions in the sidebar, organised in folders, with a colour per host. Persistent workspaces Remote processes survive SSH disconnections and app restarts. Muxscape reconnects on its own and puts every tab and pane back. SSH host management Saved hosts in folders. Hosts from ~/.ssh/config appear automatically, including Include, IdentityFile and ProxyJump. Keys, sshagent and jump hosts. Careful with secrets Host keys are checked against your OpenSSH known_hosts. Saved passwords are optional and encrypted (Argon2id, XChaCha20Poly1305) behind a master password. Built for longrunning work Editors, test watchers and coding agents like Claude Code or Codex keep running in tmux while you're away. Paste a screenshot or drop a file onto a pane and it's uploaded to the server, path typed for you. Links that just work Ctrl+click any URL in a terminal. A localhost link on the server is forwarded first, then opened. Easy on the eyes Four themes, six accent colours, adjustable text size and a colour per host so production never looks like staging. How it works 1. Step 1 Connect Add an SSH host, or pick one from your existing ~/.ssh/config. 2. Step 2 Work Open an existing tmux session, or start one. Its windows are tabs, its panes are splits. 3. Step 3 Resume Close Muxscape or drop off the network. Come back later and your workspace is exactly where you left it. There's nothing proprietary on the server. Muxscape speaks standard SSH and drives the server's own tmux through [tmux control mode](https://github.com/tmux/tmux/wiki/ControlMode). No background agent, no daemon, no account. In motion Two things that are hard to show in a still. Real recordings of the app against a real server. The connection drops. The build doesn't. Muxscape notices, reconnects on its own, and the output picks up where the server is now. Quit the app. Come back later. Your sessions reopen and everything you left running is still running. Under the hood tmux is the source of truth. Muxscape never keeps its own copy of your sessions: it asks tmux what exists, renders it, and turns every click into a tmux command. That's why another tmux client sees your changes instantly, and why there is nothing to lose when the app closes. Rust core Connections, sessions, port forwarding and the password vault, with tests that run against real SSH and tmux servers. SSH transport The russh library: keys, agent, jump hosts, keepalives, hostkey checks against known\_hosts. tmux control mode One control connection per session streams pane output and layout changes as structured events. Tauri desktop shell A small native app using the system webview, not a bundled browser. React + xterm.js Every pane is its own xterm.js terminal, sized to tmux's exact cell grid. Serverside persistence Your processes live in tmux on the server. The app can come and go. Try the alpha The first public alpha is for Windows (x64). Expect rough edges; tell us about them. Your servers need SSH and, for persistent workspaces, tmux. [Download for Windows(alpha)](https://github.com/CubezCStys/muxscape/releases/download/v0.1.0alpha.1/Muxscape%5F0.1.0%5Fx64setup.exe) Version 0.1.0 alpha for Windows 10/11 (x64), 5.4 MB, from [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/CubezCStys/muxscape/releases). SHA256 6636358f5112e2d99ccd16cdade12a5246489bdead81a43a562567db82d650dd The alpha isn't codesigned yet and is brand new, so warnings are expected. Your browser may say the file "isn't commonly downloaded" or is "suspicious": choose Keep (in Edge, open the downlo
items.author: CubezCS
items.descZh: Muxscape 是一款颠覆性的现代 SSH 客户端，其核心背景在于将服务器端持久化的复杂 tmux 会话转化为直观、可点击的图形化标签页与分屏窗格，彻底降低命令行操作的视觉与记忆负担。它不仅提供图形化的标签管理，更将拖拽、拆分、重命名等操作转化为真实的 tmux 命令，确保与原生终端的无缝同步。亮点方面，它支持跨服务器的模糊快速查找、精确适配 tmux 单元格网格的全屏渲染，并能自动识别如 localhost:5173 的本地开发端口并一键进行 SSH 转发。安全与架构上，软件采用 Rust 核心结合 Tauri 与 xterm.js，无后台依赖，并使用 Argon2id 和 XChaCha20Poly1305 协议对可选密码进行主密码加密。该产品高度适用于需要长期维护多台服务器、运行不中断的后台构建与开发任务，并追求工作状态随开随接续的专业开发者与运维工程师。
items.quote: 一款现代的 SSH 客户端，可将持久的 tmux 会话转化为可点击的标签页和窗格。

items.author: flreey
items.descZh: 该平台构建了一个无需注册即可免费下载的 CC0 音效库，拥有超过 9,700 种适用于视频、游戏和应用的无版权音频素材，支持 WAV 和 MP3 格式。核心功能包括按 23 个类别筛选、关键词搜索，以及创新的 AI Studio 功能，用户输入文字描述即可在数秒内生成 4 个候选音效。平台亮点在于其对 AI 开发工具的深度集成，支持通过 MCP 或 REST API 无密钥调用，且提供诸如平台跳跃（12种音效）、恐怖游戏（10种音效）等预制音效包，其中热门过渡风声（Transition Whoosh）在过去两周内下载量达 44 次。这使得开发者、游戏设计师和视频剪辑师能够零门槛、高效率地获取合规且精准的交互与环境音效。

items.author: reverseblade2
items.descZh: 该产品是一个名为“Hacker GitHub”的数据统计与排名平台，背景是Hacker News作为全球开发者社区重要风向标，长期讨论大量开源项目。其核心功能是聚合并量化分析2008年以来Hacker News故事和评论中提及的GitHub仓库链接，提供多维度排名与筛选。亮点在于拥有44,192个仓库的超大规模数据集，基于384,444条链接进行排名，并能按语言、年份、提及数、星标数等灵活筛选，清晰揭示社区技术热点变迁，例如Go语言仓库以1,947次提及位居榜首。该工具适用于技术趋势研究者、开源项目运营者、开发者选型参考以及技术投资人等场景，帮助他们高效捕捉社区真实关注焦点。
items.quote: 自2008年以来，根据HN故事和评论中的384,444个链接，对44,192个仓库进行了排名。
